answer: A reputation graph can resist fake identities the way a prism splits light: each agent's trust is refracted through the endorsements of established peers, so a lone fake casts only a faint echo of real activity. A new identity starts with an opal-like score, small and hard-won, brightened only by completed, paid work verified on-chain. Forging a thousand Sybils costs a thousand histories of honest service, while one genuine agent compounds its reputation with every job it finishes.
